correctness.rationale: The normalized derivative inequality gives global univalence by integrating along line segments and positivity of Jacobian. The quotient omega=g'/ (h'-alpha) is holomorphic Schur and vanishes at zero; Schwarz gives |g'|<=|z||h'-alpha|. Angular Parseval yields the exact nonnegative coefficient remainder and integrated sharp lower area inequality. Equality forces h'=1 and omega=e^{i theta}z. Positive-real-part coefficient bounds give the already-known sharp upper endpoint. Two explicit admitted families fill the interval; their r->1 limits give the full-disk spectrum. All domain and endpoint conditions are treated. The finite checker corroborates algebra but is not used as infinite proof.
